note: Size budgets for the built output. Checked by `npm run budget`, enforced in CI.
`limit` is a ceiling somebody chose. `measured` is what the build produced when
the limit was last recorded, kept beside it so the headroom is visible without
running anything. Refresh the measurements with `npm run budget:update`; that
command deliberately does NOT touch the limits.
Raising a limit is a commit with a reason. The limits below were set at the
first measurement (2026-08-14, commit b066c89) with roughly 5% headroom on the
text bundles and the asset trees. demo-css-gzip is the exception: at 7 KB, 5%
is 360 bytes and one new component's classes would trip it, so it carries a
flat ceiling instead of a percentage.

RM-003 A0 and A1 RAISED the two library limits, which needs a reason on the
record. Between them they added a resource registry, a document validator, a
load session and disposal paths across nine files - real functionality, and
about 17 KB gzipped on the IIFE. A0 alone consumed the 5% headroom the limit
was set with and A1 went 2.7 KB over it.
WHAT THAT EXPOSED, which is worth more than the limits themselves: the library
builds are `minify: false` (vite.config.mjs), so every docblock ships to every
consumer of architect3d/iife. Measured on the A1 bundle: 443.9 KB gzipped, of
which 163.4 KB - 37% - is comments. This codebase documents heavily on purpose
and that is not going to change, so the two facts do not sit well together. The
limits below are raised to fit the code that exists; whether an unminified
bundle is the right thing to publish is a separate question and a separate
change. Do not raise these again without asking it.
A2 RAISED lib-esm-gzip, and only that one. It went 0.4 KB over; lib-iife-gzip
did not go over and is deliberately left where it is, at 1.7% headroom, rather
than pre-emptively widened. A limit raised before it is breached is slack the
change did not earn - see the P6 note above - and A3 tripping this one is the
forcing function the paragraph above asks for, not an accident to smooth over.
Re-measured while raising it, and the ESM figure is worse than the IIFE one:
106.1 KB gzipped of which 55.4 KB - 52.2% - is comments. Two observations that
should shape the answer rather than delay it further:
- The IIFE is the bundle a browser downloads as written. Its 37.6% is a real
cost paid by every end user of a drop-in <script> tag.
- The ESM entry is consumed through a bundler, which strips comments on the
consumer's way to production. Its 52.2% is a transfer-and-parse cost at
install and build time, not a runtime cost - and those comments are the
JSDoc that gives a typed consumer its documentation and hover text.
So the two entries plausibly want different answers, and 'minify the library'
is the wrong shape of question. Still not this sprint's decision to make.
A3 RAISED lib-esm-gzip AGAIN, and this is the third consecutive sprint to
raise a library limit. That is the signal, not the number. A3 added assigned
identities across five entity kinds, a room matcher, item reconciliation and

lib-iife-gzip is now at 0.3% HEADROOM and was again not raised: A4 will trip
it on the next docblock, which is what a budget is for.
A4 ANSWERED IT, and the answer is split because the two artifacts have
different consumers.
- lib-iife-gzip is now MINIFIED, and its limit came DOWN from 459 KB to
233 KB - the direction P6 moved limits and the direction this one should
have moved years ago. A browser downloads this bundle as written, so its
37.6% of comments was a cost paid by every end user of a drop-in <script>
tag for documentation none of them would read. Measured by this checker:
463.7 KB to 220.8 KB, a 52.4% cut, with the source untouched and the
sourcemap still emitted. Verified rather than assumed - the minified
bundle parses, exposes all 170 exports, and its DesignRuntime still holds
the module-level configuration, dimensioning and render profile by identity.
- lib-esm-gzip stays UNMINIFIED, on purpose. A bundler strips comments on
the consumer's way to production, so its 52.2% is a build-time cost only,
and those comments are the JSDoc a typed consumer reads on hover.
The consequence of leaving the ESM unminified is that its limit tracks the
code that exists, and A4 took it 2.8 KB over. Raised to 125 KB - the fourth
consecutive sprint to move it, and now for a recorded reason rather than a
deferred one. Note what that entry actually guards, per the paragraph near
the top of this note: it is a PROPERTY check, not a size one. The ESM entry
externalises three and bezier-js, and losing that config takes it from ~118
KB to ~423 KB. Any ceiling well under 423 KB still catches that, which is the
failure it exists to catch.
What to watch now: lib-iife-gzip has stopped measuring comments and started
measuring code again. If IT starts climbing, that is a real finding about the
library's size rather than about its documentation - which is exactly what a
budget on a minified artifact is for, and what this one could not tell you
before.
A5 ADDED catalog-item-largest, which is a new KIND of ceiling rather than a
new number. public-total asks what the deployment weighs and public-largest
asks whether one file has got out of hand; neither can answer 'what happens
when somebody clicks a chair'. A catalog item is a .glb plus every image it
references plus the thumbnail already on screen, and that sum is what a user
waits for. Measured across all 168 items: the median is 17 KB and the worst
is 1.53 MB (Full Bed), which is 90x the median and was invisible to both of
the other two.
A5 also grew public-total by 58 KB - the generated asset manifest, which is

point. Draco-encoding the model catalog took public-total from 10.62 MB to 7.45
and demo-total from 17.22 to 14.39; public-largest fell from 1.30 MB to 844 KB

catalog-item-largest halved, 1.53 MB to 752 KB. Leaving the old ceilings would

lib-esm-gzip went UP, 128,000 to 134,000, and it is the entry that has been
flagged as tight since A5 landed at 0.8% headroom. The A5 note predicted this:
'the next thing that adds a docblock to the library will trip it, which is what

decoder-total is new. public/draco/ is 250,876 bytes of WebAssembly and its
wrapper, vendored from three 0.185.1, and it is inside public-total already -
but it is the only thing in that tree that is machinery rather than content. It
changes when three is upgraded and at no other time, so a line that moves for
exactly one reason is worth more than a number buried in a 7 MB total. Also a
tripwire: three ships a 719 KB pure-JS decoder beside the WASM one, and a
refresh that copied the wrong directory would show up here immediately.
texture-vram is the third KIND of budget in this file, after P6's per-file
ceiling and A5's per-catalog-item one, and it exists because B1 went looking
for the texture half of the payload and found the numbers are unrelated to the
ones already here. 202 images weigh 5.23 MB on disk and occupy 164 MB of GPU
memory once uploaded with mip chains, because an uploaded texel is four bytes
whatever the file compressed to. rooms/textures/Ground_4K.jpg is the case that
makes it concrete: 73.2 KB on disk, 16.88 MB in VRAM, 230x, and invisible to
every other line here. That is what a phone runs out of, not the download.
It is a floor rather than an exact figure - a file whose header will not parse
is skipped, so the number can only under-report, which is the safe direction
for a ceiling to sit on. KTX2/Basis is the answer and B1 did not ship it: the
encoder needs KTX-Software binaries that are not installed here, and quoting a
published ratio instead of measuring one is the thing this program refuses to
do. The arithmetic that IS measurable says BC7/ETC2 would take 164 MB to 41.

With the oversized JPEGs capped, rooms/textures/hardwood.png became the largest

decoder-total     264,000 -> 881,000   the Basis transcoder, 580 KB
lib-iife-gzip     239,000 -> 268,000   KTX2Loader, +15.4 KB gzipped

The Basis transcoder is 580 KB against Draco's 250, and that is the honest
price of the format: 22.84 MB of GPU memory for a one-time 580 KB fetch that
only happens when a compressed texture is actually loaded. It is not in the
bundle - vite.config.mjs's dropBundledCodecs() covers KTX2Loader now as well as
DRACOLoader, and without it the IIFE would have gained half a megabyte rather
than 15 KB.
public-largest ALSO CHANGED WHAT IT MEASURES, and this needs saying plainly
because it is the second time this line has been reinterpreted. It now excludes
public/draco and public/basis. The transcoder is 515 KB - four times the largest

inside a tree that was under its total. Draco's 250 KB never tripped it only
because it happened to be smaller than a JPEG. Machinery is watched by
decoder-total; this line watches content, and it now points at a .glb again.
texture-vram is at 72% headroom and is deliberately NOT lowered to 5%. The
number it reports, 12.54 MB, assumes every KTX2 transcodes to a 1 bpp GPU
format - true on any GPU with BC1, ETC1 or ASTC, which is all of them in
practice. A device with none still loads these textures correctly: Basis falls
back to RGBA8, and the figure would climb back toward 43 MB. The headroom is
that fallback, and tightening it would make the budget fail on the hardware it
is least able to help.

rather than folded in. Everything it says about the HEADROOM is right and

found it counting 174 thumbnails no GPU is asked for and the honest figure was
smaller; C1 found it counting 18 fewer textures than the tree has and the
honest figure is larger. Neither was a change to the tree. A budget that falls
because the measurement stopped looking is the failure this file exists to
catch, and it has now happened here twice.

strength of transcoding 18 model textures to KTX2/ETC1S. `npm run oracle` has
now rendered all 18 against the sources they were encoded from, and NINE of
them are past the 3.0 codec gate the project already had: nyc2.jpg at 7.00,

nobody is looking. It does not exist to make a quality regression permanent by

public-total     5.28 -> 5.84 MB against a 5.91 MB ceiling
public-largest    252 -> 307 KB  against a 322 KB ceiling  (oak_wood.jpg)
demo-total      12.44 -> 13.05 MB against a 13.22 MB ceiling
texture-vram    16.15 -> 27.38 MB, limit untouched at 45.15

sprint with a measurement in front of it, not a limit bump.
